SearchSearchFacebookTwitterEmailSMSBlue SkyWhatsappPrintRedditFlipboardPinterestLinkedinLatest StoriesPoliticsU.S. NewsWorldSportsBusinessHealthSelectedTiplineEuropeDenmark accuses Russia of plotting to kill Ukrainian American rapper on its soilTwo alleged members of an outlawed Danish gang have been arrested in connection with the attempted killing, police said.Listen to this article with a free profile00:0000:00Russia escalates attacks on Ukraine as concerns grow in Europe01:41Get more newsLiveonShareAdd NBC News to GoogleNov. 21, 2026, 5:15 AM ESTBy Reuters and The Associated PressCOPENHAGEN, Denmark — Authorities thwarted the attempted killing of a Ukrainian American citizen on Danish soil in a plot allegedly orchestrated by Russian intelligence services, the Danish prime minister’s office said Friday.

The Russian defense attaché has been expelled from Denmark in response, Danish Foreign Minister Lars Løkke Rasmussen told a news conference. Two alleged members of the outlawed Danish gang “Loyal to Familia” have been arrested in connection with the attempted killing, police said.

Danish broadcaster DR, citing a court hearing, reported the men are suspected of having been recruited to assassinate ​a Ukrainian rapper ahead of a planned performance.

Police thwarted the alleged plot when they arrested ​the two men shortly before the rapper ​Kyivstoner’s Sept. 25 concert, which was later ⁠canceled.

It was unclear how police identified the two men, who ​were stopped in ​a vehicle ⁠carrying several weapons, or how the investigation expanded to include two other men ​who are not accused of participating ​in ⁠the alleged assassination plot targeting Kyivstoner.

However, all four men have been held in custody since September, according to ⁠the ​broadcaster.

It was also unclear how ​the Russian intelligence services allegedly recruited the two Danish suspects.

Danish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said the incident is a "clear illustration of the grave security situation Denmark and Europe find ourselves in."Radek Mica / AFP via GettyDanish Prime Minister Mette Frederiksen said: “It is a clear illustration of the grave security situation Denmark and Europe find ourselves in. We are facing a Russia under pressure which is acting more aggressively and is more willing to take risks.”

The Danes’ announcement came as tensions between Europe and Russia heightened again Friday. Two Russian missiles and a suspected drone came down in Poland in what its prime minister said was likely a provocation timed to coincide with European military exercises in his country for a possible postwar mission in Ukraine.

European Commission ​President Ursula von der Leyen said on Saturday the E.U. ⁠stands in full solidarity with Denmark.

And it is unacceptable. We stand in full ‌solidarity with Denmark. ‌And with all Member States targeted by Russian ⁠hybrid attacks,” she said in an X post.

European Council President António Costa said: “We will not be intimidated. Russia’s tactics and threats will not weaken the European Union’s resolve to continue supporting Ukraine.”

The Russian Embassy in Copenhagen said on Friday the accusations were not backed ‌with proof.
